themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Several problems have no reliable answer key to check work against. So the models' first move is usually to build one: a fixed panel of buyer questions, always-dark test markets, a labeled set of known agent sessions, or a group of customers who tell you the truth about their devices.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models say there is no denominator or stable unit because answers are personalized and leave no impression logs; the same gap drives the geo switchback calendar for cross-channel incrementality, the consenting truth set for identity resolution, the labeled agent sessions for agentic traffic, and the count of certainly-identified accounts for lost B2B buying-group signal.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, an ad budget, or a buying conversation leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, model, or private chat that holds it. Compliance and effect can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models say ad platforms and trained models expose no lineage and are structurally incentivized to stay black boxes; the same opacity appears as hidden retrieval pipelines in answer engine optimization, platforms concealing their own auction changes in cross-channel incrementality, untraceable vendor side effects in safe agent execution, and private internal channels in lost B2B buying-group signal.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what a tool will do, they build one door they own and force everything through it. Gateway, proxy, shared eligibility check, spending cap, kill switch, because a sent message or a spent ad budget cannot be taken back.
themes.evidence: All three models answer safe agent execution with a broker, gateway, or intercepting proxy that hard-caps spend and audience size; the same instinct shows up as one shared pre-send eligibility check in journey orchestration, expiring daily cohorts instead of perpetual audience lists in downstream consent, and dedicated token-gated endpoints for declared agents in agentic traffic.

themes.name: Politics, Not Plumbing
themes.plain: Several problems look like missing technology but are really fights over money, ownership, and reported numbers. Teams and platforms disagree on purpose, so no schema or standard can settle whose number has to change.
themes.evidence: On the governed semantic context layer all three models call conflicting definitions of active customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap; journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for their own attributed revenue, agentic traffic lacks anyone with leverage to issue credentials everyone accepts, and identity resolution keeps losing to platforms and regulators changing the rules.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: Some of the hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and implied claims, and no rule set captures that. The models keep concluding that judgment can only be narrowed to a smaller, safer box, not automated away.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models agree that deciding whether copy makes a claim, and whether a phrasing nuance breaks its substantiation, is the very judgment the system is trying to avoid; the semantic context layer answers reach the same place, saying context-dependent meaning cannot be collapsed into one global definition.
